findings.F1: The confirmed decline after an upward breakout in a falling coin is not about the upward breakout. Downward breakouts in a falling coin are followed by nearly the same unusual 12-day move: -2.36 % (t -5.29, 1397 cases) against -2.67 % (t -5.04, 1122 cases) for upward ones. The negative 30-day return carries the effect, not the break of the two-day range.
findings.F2: The confirmation rests mostly on one year. In 2025 the unusual move after an upward breakout in a falling coin is -7.4 % (t -9.68, 252 cases). In 2018, 2020, 2023 and 2024 it is +0.4 %, +1.7 %, 0.0 % and +1.5 % (no t below -2, 460 cases together).
findings.F3: The book is mainly a bet on the market falling. Its mean daily return is positive in 2018, 2022 and 2025, the years the coins fell (coin daily mean -0.35 %, -0.26 % and -0.03 %). It is negative in 2020, 2023 and 2024, the years they rose (book -0.10 %, -0.11 % and -0.10 %). Trades lose on average in every year except 2025: mean net from -1.2 % to -13.2 %, against +3.6 % in 2025.
findings.F4: Shorting fights the coins' normal rise. Per case the unusual move is +2.55 %, but the normal drift in the short direction is -2.21 %, so a short earns only +0.34 % before costs. Trades held 13 to 20 days lost 10.5 % net on average (452 trades).

findings.F6: On the 12-day grid, the coin's next 12 days rise with its volatility-scaled 30-day return (Spearman 0.058, p 0.009, about 2070 cases).
findings.F7: The brief's premise that a narrow range comes before a larger move is absent. After a breakout, the mean absolute 12-day move is 13.0 % in the narrowest quintile of the prior two-day range and 13.4 % in the widest. On the grid it is 14.8 % in the narrowest quintile against 14.0 % in the widest, with no gradient between them.

ideas.idea: When a coin's four-hour bar closes above the high of its preceding two days while its 30-day return is positive, the coin rises more than usual over the next 6 to 24 days, and the stronger its 30-day rise relative to its volatility, the larger the further rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader should take, and hold for days, upward breakouts in a coin that is already rising over the month, rather than fade them, the more so the stronger the month's rise.
ideas.name: breakout continues in uptrend

ideas.idea: A coin's return over the next 24 days rises with its 30-day return divided by its 30-day volatility: the stronger its recent risk-adjusted rise, the more it gains over the following weeks.
ideas.consequence: A trader should hold a coin long in proportion to the strength of its volatility-scaled monthly rise, and refuse longs in coins whose month has been weak.
ideas.name: volatility-scaled monthly momentum
